title: NORTHGROVE apparel capsule: isolate an 8-SKU two-session shirt batch onto one matched white PDP set and merge per-SKU spec cards
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Freelancer.com background-removal/apparel brief (client wanted an amateur worn-shirt shot cleaned up and a 'similar shirt' isolated for a listing). The literal asks in that brief — compositing a second shirt into the scene and AI-erasing room clutter — are both on the connector's NOT-AVAILABLE list, so the job is honestly re-cast to the in-scope apparel-catalog intent the bg_removal_batch category points at, and SCALED UP to a real capsule-line workload instead of a single hero. The fictional brand NORTHGROVE (olive leaf glyph + charcoal condensed-sans wordmark) is invented for this benchmark; web search returns no confusable apparel company or trademark. 'NORTHGROVE', the eight garment names, and all copy are fictional; Adobe / Instagram / Freelancer.com are platform names, not brands in the scene. No real person, brand, product, or trademark appears anywhere in the spec.
one_line_ask: Take eight NORTHGROVE garment photos shot across two mismatched lighting days (each with a grey reference card in frame), neutralise every frame to the card so the set reads as one white point, bring the two olive SKUs and the rust SKU to a true, matched house colour, knock every garment onto a clean solid-white PDP background WITHOUT destroying the interior negative space, then vectorize the wordmark and merge one typeset spec card per SKU.
full_brief: We're a small cotton-shirt label relaunching our online store and the catalog looks like it was shot by two different people on two different days — because it was. Attached are eight garment photos: our whole autumn capsule, one shot per style, laid flat on a white sweep. Four were shot by the window on an overcast morning (they run cold and slightly blue); the other four were shot that evening under our old tungsten work lights (they run warm and orange). We dropped a standard grey reference card at the edge of every frame on purpose so you have something honest to balance against. Right now the same olive fabric looks army-drab in one photo and almost khaki-yellow in another, the whites are all over the place, and the messy sweep and the card are still in shot. What we need back: (1) every one of the eight photos corrected so the grey card reads truly neutral and the whole set sits at one consistent brightness and white point — a customer scrolling the grid should not be able to tell which shots came from which day; (2) our two olive styles (the Field Shirt and the Ridge Henley) and the Rust Canyon overshirt brought to their true, matched house colours — the olive rich and green, not muddy or yellow; the rust warm but not glowing radioactive — while keeping every wrinkle, weave and shadow looking real, no flat painted-on colour; (3) each garment cleanly lifted off its background and set on a pure solid-white PDP backdrop with the sweep and the grey card gone, and — this is where our last freelancer failed — the see-through gaps kept see-through: the space inside an open button placket, under a folded collar, between rolled sleeves must NOT get bricked in with solid white; (4) our wordmark turned into clean vector art for the woven labels; and (5) using the InDesign spec-card template and the SKU sheet we're sending, one finished product card per style with its cleaned packshot placed and its name, colourway, fabric and price set in type. Deliver the eight matched packshots at web size, the vector logo, and the eight spec cards. Please tell us, per photo, exactly what white-balance and exposure correction you landed on, so we can trust the set is genuinely matched and not just eyeballed.

inputs.name: NG101_olive_field_shirt_flatlay.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal top-down ecommerce flat-lay of a single olive-green cotton button-down field shirt, laid flat and open on a seamless white paper sweep, collar folded, one sleeve rolled so there is a clear see-through gap between the cuff and the body, the button placket slightly open showing negative space between the plackets. A standard 18-percent neutral grey reference card and a small white swatch sit flat on the sweep at the lower-left edge of the frame. Shot under COOL overcast window light with a distinct blue-cyan cast and a slightly flat, marginally under-exposed exposure. Real cotton weave, natural creases, faint soft contact shadow. Straight off the camera, un-graded, not CGI-glossy.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU NG-101, Session A (cool/blue, session-1 of two). Olive reads muddy-cold here and must be matched to the warm-session olive henley. The rolled sleeve + open placket create genuine interior negative space that a solid-fill knockout would destroy. Grey card in frame is the neutralisation target.

inputs.name: NG102_olive_ridge_henley_flatlay.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal top-down ecommerce flat-lay of a single olive-green cotton henley (same olive dye lot as the field shirt) laid flat on a seamless white paper sweep, three-button placket open at the neck showing a see-through gap, sleeves folded across the body leaving a visible gap between sleeve and hem. A standard 18-percent neutral grey reference card and a small white swatch sit on the sweep at the lower-right edge. Shot under WARM tungsten work-light with a strong orange cast and slightly bright exposure. Real waffle-knit texture, natural folds, soft contact shadow. Un-graded catalog shot, not CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU NG-102, Session B (warm/orange, session-2). Same olive garment family as NG-101 but photographed under the opposite cast — the two must end at ONE matched house olive. Warm cast pushes the olive toward khaki-yellow; the house-look HSL must pull it back to green.

inputs.name: NG103_rust_canyon_cord_overshirt_flatlay.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal top-down ecommerce flat-lay of a rust/terracotta corduroy overshirt laid flat and open on a seamless white paper sweep, chest pockets and open front placket creating interior gaps, one cuff folded back. A standard 18-percent neutral grey reference card and a small white swatch sit on the sweep at the frame edge. Shot under WARM tungsten work-light with an orange cast; the already-saturated rust corduroy is pushed near-glowing and slightly clipping in the highlights of the wale. Real corduroy wale texture and pile shadowing, soft contact shadow. Un-graded catalog shot.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU NG-103, Session B (warm). Trap for over-correction: neutralising the orange cast plus any vibrance lift makes the rust clip radioactive. The house-look pass here must RESTRAIN saturation/luminance, not boost it — the opposite move to the olive SKUs. Tests that the agent computes per-hue direction, not a blanket 'make colours pop'.

inputs.name: NG104_oatmeal_waffle_henley_flatlay.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal top-down ecommerce flat-lay of an oatmeal / warm-beige waffle-knit henley laid flat on a seamless white paper sweep, placket open at the neck. A standard 18-percent neutral grey reference card and a small white swatch sit on the sweep at the frame edge. Shot under COOL overcast window light with a blue-cyan cast, flat exposure. Real waffle texture and soft folds, faint contact shadow. Un-graded catalog shot.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU NG-104, Session A (cool). Near-neutral warm-beige fabric: the WB correction to neutralise the card must NOT tint the oatmeal fabric green or grey. Tests restraint — a correct grey-card neutralisation leaves the beige believable.

inputs.name: NG105_sand_linen_popover_flatlay.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal top-down ecommerce flat-lay of a sand / pale-tan linen popover shirt laid flat on a seamless white paper sweep, half-placket open, sleeves loosely folded with gaps. A standard 18-percent neutral grey reference card and a small white swatch sit on the sweep at the frame edge. Shot under WARM tungsten work-light with an orange cast, slightly bright. Real slubby linen weave and wrinkles, soft contact shadow. Un-graded catalog shot.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU NG-105, Session B (warm). Pale near-neutral fabric under a warm cast — must be cooled to the same neutral-daylight target as the cool-session shots without going blue. Its brightness must be pulled to the shared exposure.

inputs.name: NG106_charcoal_flannel_overshirt_flatlay.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal top-down ecommerce flat-lay of a charcoal-grey brushed flannel overshirt laid flat and open on a seamless white paper sweep, front placket open showing interior negative space, chest pocket flaps, one sleeve rolled. A standard 18-percent neutral grey reference card and a small white swatch sit on the sweep at the frame edge. Shot under COOL overcast window light, flat and slightly under-exposed so the dark flannel muddies toward black. Real brushed-flannel nap and soft folds, faint contact shadow. Un-graded catalog shot.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU NG-106, Session A (cool). Dark garment: exposure/black-point discipline — lift enough to match set brightness without crushing the charcoal to pure black or lifting it to grey. Its dark edge against the white sweep is easy to isolate; contrast with NG-107.

inputs.name: NG107_ecru_oxford_shirt_flatlay.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal top-down ecommerce flat-lay of an ecru / off-white oxford-cloth shirt laid flat on a seamless white paper sweep, collar and open placket producing subtle interior gaps, buttons visible. A standard 18-percent neutral grey reference card and a small white swatch sit on the sweep at the frame edge. Shot under COOL overcast window light with a faint blue cast, gentle exposure. Real oxford basketweave texture, soft natural creases, very soft contact shadow. Un-graded catalog shot, low contrast between the pale fabric and the white sweep.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU NG-107, Session A (cool). Hardest isolation edge in the batch: a near-white ecru garment sitting on a white sweep — very low fabric-to-background contrast, so a clean knockout demands prompt-anchored subject isolation, not a luminance guess. Also a WB restraint case (don't drive the ecru grey).

inputs.name: NG108_clay_popover_flatlay.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal top-down ecommerce flat-lay of a clay / muted-terracotta cotton popover shirt laid flat on a seamless white paper sweep, half-placket open, sleeves folded with gaps. A standard 18-percent neutral grey reference card and a small white swatch sit on the sweep at the frame edge. Shot under WARM tungsten work-light with an orange cast. Real cotton texture, natural folds, soft contact shadow. Un-graded catalog shot.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU NG-108, Session B (warm). Muted mid-chroma fabric close in hue to the rust SKU but a DIFFERENT correct answer: it only needs cast-neutralisation, no chroma restraint, so the agent must not blanket-treat the two warm reddish garments the same way.

inputs.name: NORTHGROVE_wordmark.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A clean minimalist apparel-brand wordmark reading 'NORTHGROVE' in a modern condensed sans-serif, deep charcoal letters on a transparent background, with a small simple olive-green leaf glyph to the left of the word. Flat two-colour mark, crisp hard edges, centred, generous padding, high resolution, suitable for tracing to SVG.
inputs.realism_notes: Flat two-colour text-bearing raster is exactly the clean-edged art that image_vectorize traces well to SVG. gemini-3-pro-image chosen because the mark carries legible type. Used for the woven-label vector deliverable — a real garment-brand asset need, not decoration.

inputs.name: northgrove_speccard.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED asset (client-supplied, not model-generated): a genuine single-page InDesign spec-card template (~4x6 in at 300 DPI plus bleed) with an image frame carrying an @-prefixed image-path variable and live text merge fields <<sku_name>>, <<colourway>>, <<fabric>>, <<price>>. Built as a real .indd with a data-merge source so document_merge_data_layout binds one card per row.
inputs.realism_notes: Supplied so the composed endpoint is real: a genuine authored .indd with <<fields>> AND an @-image column is the only connector-legal way to place an image into a laid-out page. The template layout is the client's; the distinctive quality of each finished card (matched packshot, preserved negative space, true colour) is the agent's work. Mirrors AO-110's supplied-.xmp pattern.

inputs.name: northgrove_capsule_skus.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED asset (client-supplied): an 8-row data-merge CSV, one row per SKU (NG-101..NG-108), with text columns sku_name, colourway, fabric, price and an @-prefixed image-path column (@packshot) whose cells must resolve to the eight isolated white-background packshots the agent produces. Header names match the <<fields>> in the .indd template.
inputs.realism_notes: The @packshot column is the binding contract: the agent must point it at its own produced packshots so document_merge_data_layout places each cleaned garment on its card. Row count = 8 fixes the page=row acceptance gate. Text-only merge (document_merge_data_vector) is explicitly the WRONG tool here because it cannot bind the image column.

outputs.name: packshots_matched_x8
outputs.spec: Eight garment packshots (NG-101..NG-108), each neutralised to its in-frame grey card and matched to ONE shared white point and brightness across the whole batch, the two olive SKUs and the rust SKU brought to their true house colours via masked luminosity-preserving HSL, then each garment isolated onto a pure solid-white PDP backdrop (#FFFFFF) with the sweep and grey card gone and all interior negative space (open plackets, under-collar, rolled-sleeve gaps) preserved — NOT solid-filled. sRGB JPEG, long edge 2048 px, and at least 300 effective DPI at the 4x6 card trim. Acceptance: on every image the grey card reads visually neutral (no colour cast; R,G,B within a tight tolerance of each other) and no white is clipped to 255 / no black crushed to 0; the agent must REPORT its final per-image white-balance (temp/tint) and exposure correction. DELIVERABLE 1 (steps produced across the per-SKU chains).

outputs.name: northgrove_logo.svg
outputs.spec: Vector SVG of the NORTHGROVE two-colour wordmark (charcoal type + olive leaf glyph) traced from the raster mark, crisp scalable paths for woven-label and card use. DELIVERABLE 2.

outputs.name: speccards_x8_pdf
outputs.spec: Eight per-SKU product spec cards, ONE PDF card per CSV row, produced by merging northgrove_capsule_skus.csv into the authored northgrove_speccard.indd via document_merge_data_layout: each card places that SKU's matched packshot through the @packshot image column and typesets <<sku_name>>, <<colourway>>, <<fabric>>, <<price>>. Acceptance gate: card/page count == data row count == 8 (a broken or empty-frame merge fails this); each placed packshot renders at >=300 DPI at the card trim. DELIVERABLE 3.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: NG101_olive_field_shirt_flatlay.jpg, NG102_olive_ridge_henley_flatlay.jpg, NG103_rust_canyon_cord_overshirt_flatlay.jpg, NG104_oatmeal_waffle_henley_flatlay.jpg, NG105_sand_linen_popover_flatlay.jpg, NG106_charcoal_flannel_overshirt_flatlay.jpg, NG107_ecru_oxford_shirt_flatlay.jpg, NG108_clay_popover_flatlay.jpg, NORTHGROVE_wordmark.png, northgrove_speccard.indd, northgrove_capsule_skus.csv
connector_workflow.note: Load the eight garment photos, the wordmark, the authored .indd spec-card template and the SKU CSV into the working project in one batch so every downstream step has real asset references. (Single upload — plumbing, not counted as difficulty.)

NG-101 (Session A, cool/blue, flat): WARM the temperature and nudge tint OFF green, and lift exposure/contrast slightly, so the in-frame grey card reads truly neutral and the frame reaches the shared brightness target. This is a per-image delta the agent must reason to from the card, NOT a batch constant — the warm-session shots need the opposite move. Agent records the temp/tint/exposure it landed on.

NG-102 (Session B, warm/orange, bright): COOL the temperature and pull exposure DOWN toward the shared target so the grey card neutralises and this warm frame matches the cool-session frames. Opposite correction sign to NG-101 — the trap is applying one set of values to all eight.

NG-103 (Session B, warm): cool to neutralise the grey card and protect the already-hot rust highlights — hold exposure/contrast so the corduroy wale does not clip before the house-look restraint pass. Record final WB/exposure.
NG-104 (Session A, cool): warm to neutral against the card WITHOUT tinting the near-neutral oatmeal fabric — restraint case; over-warming turns the beige orange. Record final WB/exposure.
NG-105 (Session B, warm, bright): cool to neutral and pull brightness down to the shared exposure without driving the pale sand linen blue-grey. Record final WB/exposure.

NG-106 (Session A, cool, dark/under-exposed): warm to neutral and LIFT exposure to the set brightness while holding the black point — charcoal must stay charcoal, not crush to 0 or wash to grey. Record final WB/exposure.

NG-107 (Session A, cool): gently warm to neutralise the card while holding the ecru near-white believable (do not grey it) and NOT clipping the whites to 255 — protecting the tonal separation the isolation step will need against the white sweep. Record final WB/exposure.
NG-108 (Session B, warm): cool to neutral against the card; muted clay needs cast-correction only — no chroma move (unlike the rust SKU it superficially resembles). Record final WB/exposure.

House-look pass, NG-101: semantically select the olive shirt fabric so the colour-truth adjustment is confined to the garment and never touches the grey card, white swatch or sweep. Returns a maskURI.

Masked luminosity-preserving HSL on NG-101's olive: rotate hue off the cold/yellow toward the house field-olive, set saturation and luminance to the shared olive target so it will MATCH the warm-session henley. Existing luminosity carries the weave and folds — this is an authored look chosen by the agent, not a preset, not auto-tone, and not image_apply_color_overlay (whole-image, would tint the sweep). Consumes the neutralised base + the mask.
House-look pass, NG-102: select the olive henley fabric only. Returns a maskURI.

Masked HSL on NG-102's olive: from the warm/khaki-yellow start, rotate hue toward green and set S/L to the SAME house field-olive target used for NG-101 so the two olive SKUs read identical across the two shooting days. Cross-asset colour match to a common target — the measurable creative core. Consumes the neutralised base + the mask.
House-look pass, NG-103: select the rust corduroy fabric only. Returns a maskURI.

Masked HSL on NG-103's rust: RESTRAIN — pull saturation down and drop the luminance of the hottest wale so the terracotta stops glowing and stops clipping, landing on the true house rust. Opposite direction to the olive passes; proves per-hue reasoning rather than a blanket 'boost colour'. Consumes the neutralised base + the mask.

Knock NG-101 onto a solid-white PDP backdrop via remove_background with backgroundColor #FFFFFF. This is the CORRECT knockout path: it isolates the garment as the foreground and preserves the interior negative space (open placket, rolled-sleeve gap) as clean white, and it removes the sweep AND the grey card. Deliberately NOT select_subject -> invert_selection -> image_fill_area: select_subject is person-only and mis-fires on a flat-lay, and fill_area solids the whole masked region, bricking the see-through gaps with white — the exact failure the brief calls out.
Knock NG-102 (matched olive henley) onto solid white via remove_background({backgroundColor:#FFFFFF}); preserve the open three-button placket gap. Same anti-pattern avoidance as step 16.
Knock NG-103 (restrained rust) onto solid white via remove_background({backgroundColor:#FFFFFF}); preserve open-front and pocket negative space.
Knock NG-104 onto solid white via remove_background({backgroundColor:#FFFFFF}); no house-look pass needed (neutral fabric), so it isolates straight from the neutralised frame.
Knock NG-105 onto solid white via remove_background({backgroundColor:#FFFFFF}); preserve half-placket and sleeve gaps.
Knock NG-106 (dark charcoal) onto solid white via remove_background({backgroundColor:#FFFFFF}); the dark garment edge cuts cleanly against white — contrast with the low-contrast ecru case in step 22.

Knock NG-107 (near-white ecru on white sweep) onto solid white via remove_background({backgroundColor:#FFFFFF}) — the hardest edge in the batch because fabric and sweep are almost the same luminance; the semantic foreground isolation (not a luminance threshold) is what makes this survivable. Preserve collar/placket gaps.
Knock NG-108 (clay) onto solid white via remove_background({backgroundColor:#FFFFFF}); preserve placket/sleeve negative space.

Resize NG-101 packshot to the shared web/card spec (long edge 2048 px, sRGB, >=300 DPI at 4x6 trim). Downscale/reframe only, never canvas-extend. Feeds both the packshots deliverable and the @packshot CSV cell for NG-101.
Resize NG-102 packshot to the shared spec; feeds NG-102's @packshot cell.
Resize NG-103 packshot to the shared spec; feeds NG-103's @packshot cell.
Resize NG-104 packshot to the shared spec; feeds NG-104's @packshot cell.
Resize NG-105 packshot to the shared spec; feeds NG-105's @packshot cell.
Resize NG-106 packshot to the shared spec; feeds NG-106's @packshot cell.
Resize NG-107 packshot to the shared spec; feeds NG-107's @packshot cell.
Resize NG-108 packshot to the shared spec; feeds NG-108's @packshot cell. Steps 24-31 are the packshots_matched_x8 deliverable and the eight image cells the merge will bind.

Trace the flat two-colour NORTHGROVE wordmark raster to clean SVG paths for the woven label and the spec cards. DELIVERABLE 2. The mark is already flat-edged 2-colour art, so it vectorizes without pre-selection (feeding a selection would return a black silhouette).

connector_workflow.inputs_from: northgrove_speccard.indd, northgrove_capsule_skus.csv, ng101_packshot, ng102_packshot, ng103_packshot, ng104_packshot, ng105_packshot, ng106_packshot, ng107_packshot, ng108_packshot
connector_workflow.note: Merge the 8-row SKU CSV into the authored spec-card .indd: the @packshot column resolves to the eight produced packshots (each placed into the card's image frame) and <<sku_name>>/<<colourway>>/<<fabric>>/<<price>> typeset per row. Emits ONE card PDF per row -> 8 cards; page=row is the acceptance gate. DELIVERABLE 3. document_merge_data_vector is the WRONG tool here (text-only, cannot bind @packshot); merging into a convert_pdf_to_indd output would silently fail to bind — both avoided.

chaining_note: One batch upload (1) fans into eight parallel per-SKU grade chains. Each SKU starts with a per-image neutralisation (steps 2-9: image_apply_adjustments, correction sign set by shooting session, computed against the in-frame grey card). Three colour-critical SKUs then take a masked house-look pass (NG-101 select_by_prompt(10)->adjust_hsl(11); NG-102 select_by_prompt(12)->adjust_hsl(13) to the SAME olive target; NG-103 select_by_prompt(14)->adjust_hsl(15) restraining rust). All eight are then knocked onto solid white with remove_background({backgroundColor:#FFFFFF}) (16-23) — the house-look SKUs consume their _house frame, the neutral SKUs consume their _neutral frame directly. Each isolated packshot is resized to the shared web/card spec (24-31), producing packshots_matched_x8 and the eight @packshot cells. The wordmark is vectorized (32). Finally document_merge_data_layout (33) binds the CSV + the eight packshots into the authored .indd, emitting one spec-card PDF per row (8 cards). Every post-upload step consumes a named prior output; the merge converges all eight packshot chains plus the template and CSV. 33 calls, 8 distinct Adobe tools.
difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon flagship rebuilt from the killed asset-prep version: 33 connector calls, 8 distinct Adobe tools, one batch upload fanning into eight dependent per-SKU chains that converge on a genuine composed endpoint (an authored-.indd data merge). Difficulty is DEPTH, not repetition: the eight neutralisations are NOT one recipe run eight times — each is a per-image WB/exposure delta whose SIGN flips by shooting session (cool session-A frames warm up, warm session-B frames cool down) and whose magnitude the agent must reason to from the in-frame grey card, so the naive move of applying one correction to all eight visibly fails the match. On top of that sit three heterogeneous masked house-look decisions in OPPOSITE directions (rotate+match the two olive SKUs to one shared target; RESTRAIN the rust so it stops clipping) plus restraint cases on near-neutral fabrics, and a low-contrast ecru-on-white isolation. The knockout must use remove_background({backgroundColor}) to keep interior negative space transparent/white — the tempting select_subject->invert->fill_area path both mis-fires (person-only selector on a flat-lay) and bricks the see-through gaps with solid white. The endpoint is a real merge with an @-image column (text-only vector merge and PDF-converted .indd both fail to bind), gated on page-count==row-count and >=300 DPI. Every step is a headless [C] connector call; no generative fill, no canvas extension, no compositing, no upscaling, no layout-by-coordinates.
hardness_rationale: FAILURE GATE: three trippable gates — (1) the in-frame 18% grey card must read visually neutral (R,G,B within a tight tolerance) AND the batch must sit at one shared white point/brightness on all eight frames, with the agent required to REPORT its per-image temp/tint/exposure, so an eyeballed or uniform correction is caught; (2) interior negative space (open plackets, under-collar, rolled-sleeve gaps) must remain white/transparent — a solid-filled knockout is a visible fail; (3) the merged deliverable must have card-count == CSV-row-count == 8 with each packshot placed at >=300 DPI. HUMAN-HARD ELEMENTS: (a) cross-asset consistency to a measurable target across eight frames shot under two opposite casts, including matching the two olive SKUs to one house olive and holding near-neutral oatmeal/ecru fabrics believable while neutralising; (b) constraint-reasoning around tool limits — knockout via remove_background({backgroundColor}) not select->invert->fill, masked recolor via image_adjust_hsl (the only masked path) not whole-image color_overlay or flat fill_area, and image placement only via a genuine @-image-column .indd merge; (c) the near-white ecru-on-white isolation edge. TRAP: the naive select_subject -> invert_selection -> image_fill_area white knockout looks right and fails twice over (person-only selector mis-fires on flat-lay garments; fill_area solids the mask and destroys the see-through gaps); a second trap is applying one WB/exposure correction to all eight frames, which the two-session cast split guarantees will not match. MEASURABLE ACCEPTANCE: grey card neutral within tolerance on every image + reported per-image WB/exposure params; the two olive SKUs land on one shared HSL olive target and the rust does not clip; packshots at long-edge 2048 px sRGB; merged cards == 8 rows at >=300 DPI at trim.
